function.description: This function is used to create a recommendation model using a given user data and an algorithm type Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

user_data.description: A data frame of user ratings. Rows represent users, columns represent items, and entries represent user ratings for items

algorithm.description: The algorithm to be used for creating the recommendation model. Collaborative filtering, content-based filtering and hybrid filtering.

matrix_factorization.description: Optional parameter to indicate whether matrix factorization should be used. Default is False.

Below is a practical, step‑by‑step guide that covers everything you’ll need to build a modern, production‑ready frontend for an e‑commerce site. Feel free to skip sections that already exist in your stack, or mix and match technologies that fit your team’s skill set. --- ## 1. Define the Scope & Architecture | Item | Why it matters | Typical tech | |------|----------------|--------------| | **Feature list** (catalog, cart, checkout, user profile, admin panel) | Keeps scope realistic | — | | **Data flow** (client ↔ API) | Determines state‑management strategy | REST, GraphQL | | **Performance goals** (first paint < 2 s, 90 % Lighthouse score) | Drives tooling choices | SSR, SSG, PWA | | **Security** (XSS, CSRF, PCI‑DSS for payments) | Protects users & business | CSP headers, HTTPS, token auth | | **Scalability** (micro‑frontend, CDN) | Future‑proof | Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare | --- ## 2. Pick a Frontend Framework | Framework | Strengths | When to choose | |-----------|-----------|----------------| | **React** (Create‑React‑App, Vite, Next.js) | Huge ecosystem, SSR/SSG, flexible | Most teams, custom needs | | **Vue** (Vite, Nuxt.js) | Simple learning curve, SSR/SSG | Small to medium projects | | **Angular** | Opinionated, built‑in services | Enterprise, strict structure | | **SvelteKit** | Zero‑runtime, fast | Performance‑centric, small bundle | > **Recommendation**: If you’re starting fresh, **Next.js** (React) gives you SSR, SSG, API routes, and a great developer experience out of the box. --- ## 3. Project Skeleton (Next.js Example) ```bash npx create-next-app@latest ecommerce-frontend --typescript cd ecommerce-frontend npm install tailwindcss postcss autoprefixer npx tailwindcss init -p ``` **Folder layout** ``` /components # Reusable UI pieces /pages # Routes (index.tsx, product/[id].tsx, cart.tsx, checkout.tsx) /lib # API helpers, hooks, context /styles # Tailwind config, global.css /public # Static assets ``` --- ## 4. UI/UX Design 1. **Wireframes** – Sketch low‑fidelity screens (Figma, Sketch, Adobe XD). 2. **Design System** – Define colors, typography, spacing, component library (Tailwind + Headless UI or Radix UI). 3. **Accessibility** – Use semantic HTML, ARIA roles, color contrast checks. 4. **Responsive Grid** – Tailwind’s `grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-3` pattern works well for product grids. --- ## 5. State Management | Option | Use‑case | Example | |--------|----------|---------| | **React Context + useReducer** | Small to medium | Cart, auth | | **Redux Toolkit** | Complex global state | Inventory, filters | | **Zustand / Jotai** | Lightweight, less boilerplate | UI toggles | | **React Query / TanStack Query** | Server state, caching | Product lists, cart sync | > **Tip**: Combine **React Query** for data fetching with **Context** for UI state. --- ## 6. API Integration ### 6.1. Fetching Data ```ts // lib/api.ts import axios from 'axios'; const api = axios.create({ baseURL: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL, headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, }); export const getProducts = () => api.get('/products'); export const getProduct = (id: string) => api.get(`/products/${id}`); export const addToCart = (productId: string, qty: number) => api.post('/cart', { productId, qty }); ``` ### 6.2. Server‑Side Rendering / Static Generation ```tsx // pages/product/[id].tsx export async function getStaticPaths() { const { data } = await getProducts(); return { paths: data.map((p: any) => ({ params: { id: p.id.toString() } })), fallback: 'blocking', }; } export async function getStaticProps({ params }) { const { data } = await getProduct(params.id); return { props: { product: data } }; } ``` --- ## 7. Shopping Cart Flow 1. **Add to Cart** – Update local state + sync with backend via API. 2. **Persist Cart** – Store in `localStorage` or `IndexedDB` for offline support. 3. **Checkout** – Redirect to payment gateway (Stripe, PayPal). ```tsx // components/CartButton.tsx import { useCart } from '../lib/cartContext'; export default function CartButton() { const { cartCount } = useCart(); return ( ); } ``` --- ## 8. Payment Integration (Stripe Example) ```tsx // pages/checkout.tsx import { loadStripe } from '@stripe/stripe-js'; const stripePromise = loadStripe(process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY!); export default function Checkout() { const handleCheckout = async () => { const stripe = await stripePromise; const { data } = await api.post('/create-checkout-session', { cartItems }); const result = await stripe.redirectToCheckout({ sessionId: data.sessionId }); if (result.error) alert(result.error.message); }; return ; } ``` > **Security**: Keep your secret keys in server‑side environment variables; never expose them in the client bundle. --- ## 9. Performance & SEO | Technique | How | |-----------|-----| | **Image Optimization** | Next.js `next/image` automatically lazy‑loads and serves WebP. | | **Code Splitting** | Automatic with Next.js; use dynamic imports for heavy components. | | **Critical CSS** | Tailwind’s `@apply` + PurgeCSS removes unused styles. | | **SSR/SSG** | Pre‑render product pages for SEO. | | **PWA** | Add `next-pwa` plugin; service worker caches assets. | | **Analytics** | Google Analytics, Plausible, or Fathom. | --- ## 10. Testing | Layer | Tool | Example | |-------|------|---------| | **Unit** | Jest + React Testing Library | Test component rendering | | **Integration** | Cypress | End‑to‑end checkout flow | | **Visual** | Storybook | Document UI components | | **Performance** | Lighthouse CI | Automated Lighthouse checks | ```bash npm install --save-dev jest @testing-library/react @testing-library/jest-dom ``` ```tsx // __tests__/ProductCard.test.tsx import { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react'; import ProductCard from '../components/ProductCard'; test('renders product title', () => { render(); expect(screen.getByText(/Test Product/i)).toBeInTheDocument(); }); ``` --- ## 11. Deployment & CI/CD | Platform | Features | Typical Workflow | |----------|----------|------------------| | **Vercel** | SSR, SSG, Edge Functions | GitHub → Vercel → Auto‑deploy | | **Netlify** | Build hooks, Functions | GitHub → Netlify → Deploy | | **Render** | Docker, Cron jobs | GitHub → Render → Deploy | | **Docker + Kubernetes** | Full control | Dockerfile → Helm chart → K8s cluster | **Example GitHub Actions** ```yaml name: CI on: push: branches: [main] pull_request: jobs: build-test: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v3 - uses: actions/setup-node@v3 with: node-version: '20' - run: npm ci - run: npm run lint - run: npm run test - run: npm run build ``` --- ## 12. Security Checklist | Item | Action | |------|--------| | **HTTPS** | Enforce via CDN or reverse proxy | | **CSP** | `Content-Security-Policy` header | | **XSS** | Escape all user input, use `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` sparingly | | **CSRF** | SameSite cookies, CSRF tokens | | **PCI‑DSS** | Use hosted payment fields (Stripe Elements) | | **Rate Limiting** | Protect API endpoints | | **Audit** | Regular dependency updates (`npm audit`) | --- ## 13. Optional Enhancements | Feature | Why | Tech | |---------|-----|------| | **Progressive Web App** | Offline shopping | `next-pwa` | | **Server‑Side Search** | Fast filtering | Algolia, ElasticSearch | | **Personalization** | Recommendations | Machine‑learning API | | **Multi‑Language** | Global reach | i18next, next‑i18next | | **Analytics Dashboard** | Business insights | Chart.js, D3 | | **Chatbot** | Customer support | Intercom, Drift | --- ## 14. Quick Reference: Sample Component ```tsx // components/ProductCard.tsx import Image from 'next/image'; import Link from 'next/link'; import { useCart } from '../lib/cartContext'; interface Props { id: string; title: string; price: number; imageUrl: string; } export default function ProductCard({ id, title, price, imageUrl }: Props) { const { addItem } = useCart(); return (

{title}

${price.toFixed(2)}

); } ``` --- ## 15. Resources & Further Reading | Topic | Resource | |-------|----------| | **Next.js Docs** | https://nextjs.org/docs | | **React Query** | https://react-query.tanstack.com/ | | **Tailwind CSS** | https://tailwindcss.com/docs | | **Stripe Integration** | https://stripe.com/docs/stripe-js | | **Accessibility** | https://www.w3.org/WAI/standards-guidelines/wcag/ | | **Performance** | https://web.dev/optimize-performance/ | | **Security** | https://owasp.org/www-project-top-ten/ | --- ### Final Checklist Before Launch 1. ✅ All critical paths (browse → add to cart → checkout) tested end‑to‑end. 2. ✅ Lighthouse score ≥ 90 (performance, accessibility, best practices). 3. ✅ HTTPS + CSP headers set. 4. ✅ API keys stored in server‑side env vars. 5. ✅ CI pipeline builds, lints, tests, and deploys automatically. 6. ✅ Analytics and error monitoring (Sentry, LogRocket) integrated. Good luck building your e‑commerce frontend! If you hit a specific roadblock—be it state‑management, payment flow, or deployment—just let me know and I can dive deeper into that area.
